status: Numerically executed rigid-frame spring-support comparison; hypothetical support positions and stiffness, NOT physical fastener/contact FEM

inputs.coordinate_system: front external x right z up; y back; all lengths mm

A_carrier.description: 8 exterior-face backer anchors around the driver, all into unmeasured MDF; no proven 3D carrier geometry
A_carrier.unknown_interface: A steel/aluminum shaped backer is assumed infinitely stiff; those points are hypothetical anchors, not a validated carrier assembly.

B_brace_rails.description: top/bottom rails plus two hypothetical direct anchor points at first brace x448-470, y unknown
B_brace_rails.unknown_interface: x451 anchors overlap the existing first brace projection and require a 3D end joint; load transfer and stiffness are unmeasured.

warnings: Anchor points are candidate positions only; no CAD 3D proves screws, frame, basket, clamp heads or module path can coexist.
The carrier and rails are modeled as INFINITELY RIGID, joined to bilateral linear springs; real beam/carrier bending, contact, tension-only constraints and MDF delamination not included.
Spring k0=100/300/1000 N/mm and multipliers 0.5/1/3/10 are uncertainty SCENARIOS, not measured MDF/brace properties.
Negative normal reactions are assumed possible; real preloaded flange/gasket may open or re-distribute load.
Acceleration 1/5/10g is hypothetical research exploration, not approved transport/safety specification.
No strength, SF, screw size, breakage or CNC release can be derived.
